paragraphs.text: deceiving not only herself but multitudes of senseless people along with her, like cattle, without knowledge [?] of the Scriptures.

It is only because of pride, as I said before, and disobedience that all these multitudes go down to Amente, whether man or woman. For indeed it was because of pride and disobedience, as we said before, that the devil was cast out of the heavens in the beginning.
Who then will be able to count, from the beginning, those who have perished and gone down to the pit,
because they walked in the way of pride and lived in disobedience?
For indeed, after all the things the Lord said from the beginning, whether in parables or in plain words, the last of all the words he spoke was this:
"Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear." Does not everyone have ears? Or has there ever been a person without ears?
Does not the creator of the universe, the King, Christ, know that he never created a person without ears?
So what is this saying he spoke: "Whoever has ears, let him hear"?
It is because he knows that the pride in people is an abomination before God, as he said.
That is why he said, "Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear": because of the disobedience
and the pride of which Scripture spoke: "My people did not listen to my voice,
and Israel paid no heed to me.
So I let them go according to the desires of their hearts;
they will walk in their own works." And again, because of pride and disobedience the Lord said in anger:
"I have begotten sons and raised them up,
but they have despised me. The ox knows its owner, and the donkey its master's manger,
but Israel has not known me, and my people has not understood me." And again, because of pride and disobedience the Lord threatened these people at that time:
"I sent to you all my servants the prophets, by day and early in the morning;
I sent them, and they did not listen to them, nor did they incline their ear,
but they walked in the thoughts of their evil heart."
Again, because of pride, Scripture was indignant with these people from the beginning:
"The sin of their mouth,
the word of their lips—let them be caught in their pride;
their end will be proclaimed from their cursing." We have said these things knowing that, as the root of every evil is love of money according to the words of the Scriptures,

so also the root of every evil is disobedience, again according to the words of the Scriptures—and above all in those who harbor hatred toward their neighbors to the very end, who carry out their murders in their heart instead of with their hands.
In the beginning the Lord spoke with Adam, making a covenant with him when he created him, putting the whole creation that is upon the earth into his hands and those of his seed,
and establishing with him and his seed an everlasting covenant, saying, "Increase and multiply and fill the earth and have dominion over it.
The fear and dread of you shall be upon all the wild beasts, and upon all the cattle of the field and all the birds of the sky, and upon all the fish of the sea.
I have put them into your hands; they shall be food for you; like the green herbs I have given them to you.
Only [flesh?] with the blood of its life you shall not eat.
For indeed your blood, the blood of your lives, I will require.
I will require it from the hand of all the beasts." Will God then judge the beasts?
Or do beasts have hands, as he said,
"I will require it from the hand of the beasts"?
No, but God knew from the beginning that many people would change and take on the nature of beasts by allowing the devil to dwell in them, so that he might carry out his murders through them,
as Cain did before the flood came. That is why he added the saying, "Whoever sheds the blood of a man,
his own shall be shed in return"—truly, according to the words of the Scriptures.
There are many people than whom the beasts are better. For beasts, this is their nature;
but people who have changed have taken on a beastly heart, which is not their nature.
Listen again to Scripture; it will tell us that there are many people who take on a human appearance outwardly, while inwardly they are beasts,
like the devil, who takes the appearance of an angel of light though he is darkness
and a murderer.
For indeed Paul wrote about the people of Crete: "They are always liars, evil beasts,
gluttonous bellies." He also speaks fully about the matter of people who have changed in their nature into a beastly nature,
when he says, "If, humanly speaking, I fought with beasts at Ephesus."
Did the holy apostle really fight with actual beasts at Ephesus?
No, they were people who had the form of beasts instead of human beings.
The Lord of glory, Jesus, speaking with his holy apostles, says concerning those who have the form of beasts instead of human beings:
"Behold, I am sending you out like sheep in the midst of wolves.
So be wise as serpents
and innocent as doves. Beware of men"—that is, of those who have the form of beasts instead of human beings.
"For they will hand you over to councils, and in their synagogues they will flog you."
For the race of those beasts will not cease until the end of the age,
and neither will the race of the blessed sheep of the flock of the good shepherd, Christ, cease until the end of the age.
This is especially true of that sort of people who live in idleness, as it is written, "Every idle man is full of desires."
If Scripture said, "Be still and know that I am God," it does not give anyone leave not to work for the life of his soul, and for food and clothing;
rather, it means: be still from the works of the flesh, which are fornication, idolatry, sorcery, enmity, strife, jealousy, contentiousness, division, factions, slander,
drunkenness, and things like these.
If those who do these things will not enter the kingdom of heaven,
neither will they know that God is God, as Scripture said:
"Be still and know that I am God." For indeed, unless a person turns away
and ceases from the works of lawlessness,
he cannot do the works of righteousness,
as the Lord said: "No one can serve two masters;
for either he will love the one and hate the other, or he will hold to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve God and mammon."
And if the Lord also said, speaking with the Jews at that time, "Do not labor for the food that perishes, but for the food that endures to eternal life,"
the King and Son of the King was not speaking—
God and Son of God—about food and clothing, as though a person should not work for what he needs. We work so that we may not be a burden
or a trouble to any of you, by having you provide for us out of what is yours [?]. How then, now,
can anyone say that he will be able to keep his life safe without working, when the Lord himself charged Adam from the beginning, when he placed him in paradise, to work it and to keep it?
For indeed he did not leave him without work and without keeping, even while his labors were still unimpaired [?], as it is written:
"With all watchfulness keep your heart,
for from these are the ways of life."
And after he cast him out of paradise he did not leave him idle without work,
but he said to him, "You shall eat the grass of the field by the sweat of your face,"
and, "You shall eat your bread until you return to the earth." Which living person did God ever blame, from the beginning,
for working for their food and clothing? Rather, Scripture has blamed idleness from the beginning, and says:
"For we hear that some among you are living in idleness, doing no work at all, but are busybodies.
Such people we command, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, to work quietly and eat their own bread"; and again, "Whoever does not work, let him not eat."
Or which of all the saints does Scripture not point out to us,
recounting the occupation of each one and setting them before us as a pattern in their work? Cain and Abel, the first offspring: did not the one become a shepherd while the other worked the earth?
Yet God did not blame Abel for tending sheep,
nor was he angry with Cain for working the earth;
rather, it was Cain's lawlessness that dishonored him,
and Abel's righteousness that honored him. And again Noah, to whom the Lord spoke:
"You are the one I have seen to be righteous before me in this generation."
Scripture bears witness about him: "Noah was a man, a farmer;
he began to plant a vineyard."
Then again the great Abraham, with whom God made a covenant to multiply his seed like the stars of heaven

and like the sand on the seashore, which is without number, and that his seed should inherit the cities of their enemies, and that all the nations should be blessed in him—as we know that the Old and the New came about in him and in his seed.
And we have found it written about him that Abraham planted a field at the Well of the Oath,
and called upon that place in the name of the Lord, the everlasting God. Was Abraham not a sower,
and a reaper? Otherwise, would he have planted at the Well of the Oath after he had made a covenant with Abimelech? As it is written about him:
"Now Abraham was very rich in cattle, in silver, and in gold."
Then Lot: did he not lift up his eyes and see that the whole region of the Jordan was well watered, and settle there with his flocks,
for they were many?
This is the one whom God saved from the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah, together with his wife and his children.
Or is it not written about Isaac that he sowed in that year
and reaped a hundredfold of barley?
Then again Jacob, whom God blessed for the sake of Abraham his father and Isaac: does he not himself say,
"I was burned by the heat of the day and by the frost of the night;
sleep fled from my eyes";
or, "Behold, for twenty years to this day I have tended your sheep"?
Did the Lord withhold his blessing and not bless him, or did he fail to multiply his seed, because he was in the field all the time?
Not only did God bless him, but his angels too were with him among the sheep,
as they appeared to him in a dream: "Lift up your eyes and see the rams mounting the white ones, the [?], and the speckled ones,
and the ash-colored and spotted ones leaping upon the sheep and the goats;
for I have seen what Laban has been doing to you."
For indeed not only were the angels with him among the sheep, but they also walked with him on the road, guiding him as he went up to Canaan, the land in which he was born,
just as, when Jacob lifted up his eyes, he saw the camp of God that had come up to him,
and the angels of God met him.
When he saw them he said, "This is the camp of God,"
and he called the name of that place "The Camp."
Or who was it that rebuked Laban as he ran after him in pursuit,
he and his brothers: "Take care that you do not speak evil to Jacob"?
For Laban spoke to Jacob when he met him: "You have carried off my children like captives taken by the sword;
you did not think me worthy to kiss my sons and my daughters. Now you have acted foolishly.

And now my hand has the power to do you harm; but the God of your father said to me yesterday, 'Take care that you do not speak evil to Jacob.'" Likewise Jacob in turn spoke to Laban when he contended with him: "Had not the God of my father Abraham been with me,
and the Fear of Isaac, you would have sent me away empty now;
but God saw my affliction and the labor of my hands,
and he rebuked you yesterday."

We have said these things so that we may know that not only did angels walk with him, but the Lord too was not far from him, being with him in every place he went, just as he spoke with him on another occasion, when he appeared to him as he was going down to Egypt, being with him:

"And I will bring you up again at the end, and Joseph will lay his hand upon your eyes." Then again the sons of Jacob, whose seed God multiplied like the stars of heaven and like the sand on the seashore, which is without number:
were they not in the field tending their father's sheep, as when Jacob called Joseph
and sent him: "Go and see whether your brothers and the sheep are well, and bring me word," sending him from the valley of Hebron?
And he came to Shechem, where a man found him wandering in the field and asked him, "What are you looking for?"
He said, "I am looking for my brothers. Tell me where they are tending the flock."
He said to him, "I heard them say, 'Let us go to Dothan.'"
We have said these things because God will not dishonor a person for being in the field doing his work for his food and clothing while pleasing God;
nor will he honor a person because he is shut in as an ascetic, if he is idle and does not work with his hands, and above all if he does not please God with good works
and good deeds. Rather, it is better for the one in the field to please God, so that God may bless him
and also bless the produce of his land.

And it is right too for the one who is shut in as a monk and as an ascetic to work with his hands for his food and clothing, and to do the will of God in works of piety, so that he may receive a blessing from the Lord on earth
and find mercy before God on the day of his visitation.
For we say these things so that we may know that God loves everyone who fears him and hopes in his name, and everyone who works with his hands, so that he may have
[?] money. And fornication and theft, and lying and false oaths, are plainly visible in the person who commits them,
and those around him and those who live with him come to know of it or catch him at it many times. But the one who hates his neighbor,
or who bears a grudge against his neighbor, keeps these things inside, in the heart, and they are not visible to their neighbors and those who live with them.

Just as the devil and his demons of darkness are hidden in what they do out of hatred for the whole human race, so too is the one who bears a grudge against his neighbor and hates him: his evil deeds are hidden within him,
and day and night alike are dark to him in the inner chamber of his heart, because his deeds are not visible.

That is why the Holy Spirit, knowing that this is a great abomination beyond all lawlessness, said concerning those who do these things: "Those who speak words of peace with their neighbor while there is enmity in their heart, and jealousy and hatred:
give to them according to their works and according to the wickedness of their thoughts;
give them their recompense." Will he give them [?]? Or what is their recompense? He will lay upon them the curse that they loved
and make it a crown upon their head.
The words that [?]
you will be able to uproot them and bring them to nothing.
O blessed are you, O love of humanity, you who are adorned with every kind
of virtue of the Spirit, you who go to stand before Christ to receive what you deserve in the places of rest in heaven!
For their likeness is not a human likeness,
but
[?] a person is deceit.
As for rejoicing at the destruction of your neighbor, the Scripture of God stands against it,

and against what it has said from the beginning about those who do these things, bringing them down and casting them out as though they did not exist, at the time and hour when it gives up its spirit into the hands of the one who hates it [?]—
Christ—together with all its other works of bitterness, as it is written: "Whoever rejoices over one who is perishing will not escape evil."

For indeed, when the Lord became human among human beings—God and Son of God—it was he who gave the law to Adam in paradise not to eat from the tree; it was he who gave the law to Abraham of the circumcision of the flesh, together with his household; it was he who spoke with Moses at the bush, having performed all those mighty works through his rod. This is the rod about which he spoke to Moses: "Take this rod in your hand,

with which you will perform all the signs"—and he accomplished them before Pharaoh and all the Egyptians by the power of his arm, as it is written: "He who brought Israel out of the land of Egypt with a strong hand and an exalted arm."
It was he who gave the law to Moses in the wilderness, and through whom every commandment and every law came into being;
he who showed mercy far, far beyond what we can tell, whose powers are beyond measure and whose wonders have no end. When, then, he became human among human beings—he being God and Son of God—
a lawyer came up to him
and asked him, to test him, "Which is the great commandment in the law?"
The Savior of truth, Jesus, answered him:
"Hear, O Israel: the Lord your God is one.
You shall love the Lord
your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength and with all your thoughts,
and your neighbor as yourself." He answered him, "Well
have you said that God is one and there is no other besides him,
and that you shall love him with all your heart and all your strength and with all your understanding.
This," he said, "is better than all burnt offerings and sacrifices."
And when the Lord of glory knew that he had honored love of humanity as it deserves, he granted him the kingdom of heaven without hesitation:
"You too are not far from the kingdom of heaven."
But he, wanting to learn the perfection of love of humanity so that he might receive greater honor,
asked him, "Who is my neighbor?" The King of powers answered him, teaching him the perfection of the straight way: "A man went down from Jerusalem to Jericho
and fell into the hands of robbers, who stripped him naked and beat him;
they went off and left him half dead.
By chance a priest came down by that road;
he saw him and passed by.
But a Samaritan came down by that road; he saw him and had compassion on him.
He went up to him and bound up his wounds;
he poured wine and oil on him and set him on his own animal;
he brought him to an inn and took care of him. The next day, as he was leaving, he gave four silver pieces
to the innkeeper and said to him, 'Take care of him,
and whatever you spend on him, I will repay you when I come back.' Which of these three
proved," he said, "a neighbor to the man who fell into the hands of the robbers?"
He said to him, "The one who showed him mercy."
And the Lord of glory, Jesus, said to him, "You too go and do likewise."

This is so that we may know that we have said nothing foreign, in anything we have said, outside of Scripture; and again, so that we may know that love is love of humanity, and love of humanity is love.
If he granted the kingdom to this man because he spoke the truth in his answer, that love of humanity is better than all burnt offerings and sacrifices,
then the one who fulfills it in his heart,
together with all the other works of righteousness—how greatly he will honor him,
and how surely he will grant him the kingdom of heaven!
So let us not boast, my brothers, that we are Christians, while there is jealousy or strife or hatred in our heart toward our neighbor,
or while we do not love our neighbor as ourselves
and do not carry out the deed;
it is a very empty name that we are called by.
The holy apostle cries out: "For where there is jealousy and strife among you, are you not carnal,
and walking in a merely human way?"
What then shall we say on the day of our visitation, since we did not know what state we were in before the days of our life came to an end?
We shall mourn in the place of mourning, where many have mourned from of old,
and we shall weep in the place of weeping, where many have wept since the beginning.
If, because of you, O love of humanity and love, this whole multitude will receive glory when the King comes in his glory with all his angels, as we said before,
and they enter into eternal life,

blessed are you, and blessed is the Lord of glory, Jesus, who sowed you for himself in the heart of the wise, so that they may inherit eternal life in all honor and all glory, with great boldness in the heavens.
And if, because of you in turn, O hatred of humanity, this whole multitude and these many peoples, from of old until now and until the end of the age, will receive shame

when the King comes in his glory to judge between these and those—between those on the right, because of love and mercy and perfect love of humanity, and those on the left, because of jealousy and hatred and mercilessness—
cursed is the one who sowed you:
the devil, who sowed you for himself as an evil seed in the heart of the foolish.

For it is he, the dragon, who made them drink the abundance of poisons that comes out of his mouth, until he had made very many drunk, without their knowing that he had led them astray from the way that goes to the city of their dwelling, bringing them out of the light into the darkness, without their knowing that it was darkness
that they were walking in, as it is written:
"Whoever hates his brother is in darkness and walks in darkness,
and does not know where he is going, because the darkness has blinded his eyes"—
until they hear that voice full of wrath which comes out of the mouth of the Almighty Jesus when he calls them to account for what was required of them,
according to the ordinance of judgment written in the Gospels,

which he made known to us beforehand, he who does not wish anyone of his creation to perish: "This is how I will do when I come, according to the deserving of those on the right, according to their works in every kind of love of humanity";
and again: "This is the ordinance for those on the left, when he comes, according to their deserving:

Receive now, O wretched and miserable ones, together with the one you loved and with whom you worked in jealousy and hatred and in utter mercilessness, in the fire of Gehenna—not for days and years, but for ages of ages."
For these things will happen at the end of the age, and there will be no further judgment after this,
nor any further day to look for with regard to a resurrection, after he has judged the angels and after he has passed sentence on the fulness of all lawlessness
and sent them in the fury of his wrath down to Amente—whether those of the angels whom he led astray, or those of the children of men whom he led astray.
The angels will [?] them all:
everyone who clings to the lawless deeds of the son of perdition, who did not repent before they died nor come out of them before the day of their visitation.
In a word, all who stand on the left, so that they may cast them down to Amente and they may inherit the Gehenna of fire forever.
O what turmoil there will be on that day for those who stand on the left, in the presence of those on the right who are in glory!
O what weeping there will be on that day among all the nations who did not know God, and all the heretics, each according to the error into which the deceiver led them astray!
But on that day people who say of themselves, "We are Christians," will be in great poverty and great misery,
not having known the calling with which they were called, nor the grace that reached them—

especially those who bear the name and the habit and live in the holy places, yet they too cling to these things in that wrath, because they did not listen to the voice of the Scriptures, which went out over all the earth,
and its life-giving words, which reached the ends of the world, crying out: "Flee from fornication.
Every sin a person commits," it says, "is outside the body,
but the one who commits fornication sins against his own body.
Or do you not know that whoever joins himself to a prostitute is one body with her,
but whoever joins himself to the Lord is one spirit with him? Or do you not know that you are the temple of God and that the Spirit of God dwells in you? Or that whoever defiles the temple of God,
God will destroy him?"
What then will happen after the outcry of these people and after the mourning of those on the left in great fear, while the ministering angels
surround them with rivers of fire, as the sentence of the Almighty Jesus comes out of his mouth, pursuing them in wrath and terror:
"Depart from me,

you cursed, into the eternal fire, which was prepared for the devil and his angels, because you did not do what I commanded you. Not only did you fail to love your neighbor, because the work was burdensome to you—
why then did you go so far as to hate him, turning judgment into gall and the fruit of righteousness into bitterness?
You have turned what I told you into what I never said, in every kind of lawlessness.

Receive now according to what you deserve and according to the wickedness of your works, in the fire of Gehenna, together with the one who turned your will into hatred, your love into mercilessness, and your purity into defilement and into fornications, into a [?] of a kind that is shameful to speak of and disgraceful to hear; the one who turned perfect piety into the perfection of every impiety in the days when you were upon the earth.
You did not listen to me when I cried out through the mouth of my servants."

the prophets: "Return to me, that you may live, you who are from the ends of the earth"; or "Return to me, that I may heal your wounds"; or "Come out from among them and separate yourselves from them."
And: "I will receive you to myself, for I am merciful"; or "I will be your God, and you will be my people."
And: "I will be a father to you, and you will be my sons and daughters."
For if the one who is pure and those whom he purifies are all from one, according to the scriptures, that is, from God,

is it not also true that the one who is defiled, the devil, and those whom he defiles are all from one, that is, from him? Whether demons, or all the unclean spirits of error that are with him, or prostitutes, or men who are worthless in every way, they all come from him, from the devil: everyone who sins in any way at all.

What, then, will happen after the judgment of the Almighty is completed, the judgment of Jesus, the Son of the Almighty Sabaoth, seated upon the cherubim, with the seraphim of light standing beside him, together with the holy archangels, in great glory, and with all his saints? For it is written, "The saints will judge the world."
They will drag all the wicked down to Amente with the devil, and repay him together with them, and repay them together with him.
How, then, should we keep these things in mind from this moment on, in the presence of God?

O the great grief of heart, and the great sorrow, for anyone who understands the things that will happen on that day, because we did not listen to the scriptures but forgot their words and put them behind us,
taking on hardness of heart and negligence until these things overtake us, though it was not our wish that they should overtake us.
And we end up in them, though it was not our wish to be in them. Did the Lord not say,
"Whatever you want people to do for you, you too
do the same for them.
For this is the Law and the Prophets"?
Indeed, the good Savior did not hide from us the fact that the gate is wide
and the road that leads to destruction is broad.
Nor did he neglect to tell us about the other one, that it is small and narrow.
He went on, moreover, to establish the work of kindness to others, putting anger and hatred to shame.

He says, "But I say to you: love your enemies, and pray for those who persecute you, so that you may become children of your Father in heaven; for he makes his sun rise on the good and the evil, and sends rain on the righteous and the unrighteous.
For if you love those who love you," he said, "what is your reward? Do not the tax collectors do the same? And if you greet only your brothers, what more are you doing? The Gentiles too,
do they not do this?
Be perfect, then, as your Father in heaven is perfect."
The holy Baptist, John, cried out from the beginning, since he had been sent
before him, pointing the people toward kindness and love.

Since among all the virtues there is none greater than these, when the crowd came out to be baptized by him and asked him what they should do, he told them, "Whoever has two tunics, let him give one to the one who has none; and whoever has bread, let him do the same."
The holy apostle, too, whom the Lord sent to preach the gospel,
cries out, "Let brotherly love
continue.
Do not neglect hospitality, for through it some have entertained angels without knowing it."
What, then, is greater than kindness to others, as we have said many times, and love? How exceedingly beautiful it is!
For mercy is its garment, and the fulfillment of the commandments of life
is a crown upon its head. It strikes great fear into the enemies as it makes its way to God,

and the devil is always troubled before it, full of shame in its presence, seeing the likeness of Christ that it wears and the sign of his holy cross; for it was because of his kindness and his compassion toward humankind that he endured the cross.
For he rebukes through the prophet;
he speaks with a threat about the kind of people whose hearts are full of deceit while they speak pleasantly with their neighbor:
behold, a true wrath before God for those who walk in this way of life. How far, then, does the judgment of such people reach? It reaches to the pit of Amente.
Since we have spoken about the prophet,

he says in the fury of his wrath, as we said before, "Behold, I will refine them." Where will he refine them? "And I will test them, for I will act in the face of the wickedness of the daughter of my people.
Their tongue is a piercing arrow.
The words of their mouth are deceitful; they speak peaceful words to their neighbors, while enmity and hatred are in their hearts. Shall I not, upon these,
bring a reckoning, says the Lord? Or on such a people as this shall my soul not take vengeance?"
This is so that we may know that all the words of scripture have opposed this way of life from the beginning,

the Old and the New. Now, since we know everything—our death and our life, our fullness and our want, how we go rightly to God by keeping what he has said with wisdom, and how we go down to Amente by transgressing what he has said in folly—

let us therefore take thought now, in the midst of these things and the others, before the day comes which we do not know and the hour which we do not know, when we shall receive according to our works, each one according to his worth and according to the fruit of his works.
O blessed are those people because of whom God will be glorified through their good deeds, who are the fragrance of Christ.
O woe to those people because of whom the name of their fathers will be reviled through their ignorance.
The good Savior teaches us, "Do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing,

when you do an act of mercy." And how well he put it! Yet, revealing again the deeds of the good person, he says elsewhere, "Let them see your good works and glorify your Father in heaven." Is it not, then, impossible for the deeds of the good person to be hidden?

For it is like a man who has the fragrance of incense inside his house, spreading far and wide: he cannot stop its fragrance, so as to keep people from smelling the fragrance inside his house when they pass by.
In the same way, no one who does good deeds and good works before God can hide them so that people do not know of them,
whether by night or by day; he cannot hide them, just as the Lord said, "There is nothing hidden that will not be revealed."
Again, it is like a man who has a great stench in his house, spreading far and wide. It does not please him, nor is it his wish that people should smell it when they pass by,

but it cannot be helped because of the overwhelming stench. So it is with the person who does deeds that do not please God and are abominations in the sight of people, even if he does them by night in the dark:
they must be revealed, as the apostle said, "Those that are otherwise cannot be hidden."

Strive, therefore, beloved brothers, and let us complete the work for whose sake we have gathered together, which is purity, along with the other commandments given to us by God through our holy father, so that we may receive glory on earth in the sight of the good and the wicked,
and so that they may glorify us even more in heaven, in the presence of God and all the saints,
and we may receive the reward for the good works we did on earth, in the metropolis of the heavens, the Jerusalem of heaven [?], of every good thing.
For our holy father Apa Athanasius says, "Keep the honorable image of the human being; for they will not call you human," he says, "if you do the works of the brute beasts."

Now then, beloved brothers, dear to us in the Lord, we have great cause to boast about you wherever we go, as people boast to us about you and tell us of your deeds before we hear them: "Behold, a chosen people, adorned

with wisdom, fearing God, and keeping the commandments of their fathers! We do not hear of war among them, nor the noise of war; rather, they spread the fame of their faith everywhere." Even those outside, who do not live with us—will they know how each of us is

in his deeds? No, but they see the power that surrounds us, and the fragrance of the righteousness of our fathers that shines around our congregation, shining brighter than the sun and more fragrant than any incense. Because of this they glorify us all the more and add to our good name.
If we do a little, they proclaim it many times over and tell one another of a host of good things that we do.
Truly we are put to shame, and become as nothing, at the things they say about us outside.
Now then, brothers, let us be firm like a city whose walls are strong and whose gates are shut.
For indeed the scriptures have said, "Like a city whose walls are broken down,
so is a man who does not act with counsel."
What counsel, then, is this of which scripture speaks, if not the counsel of God? As it is written,
"There are many thoughts in a man's heart,
but it is the counsel of God that stands firm."
"A human being is a great thing," it says, "and a merciful human being is precious."
I too, this wretched and poor one, will say this:
a human being is a great thing, and a holy human being is choicer still.
Let us therefore complete the work of godliness in every respect, whether in all the spiritual works or in the bodily ones, in the work of our hands, so that we may receive a blessing from the Lord
and mercy from God our Savior, and so that they may say of us,
"This is the generation of those who seek the Lord."
Love one another, then, my beloved brothers, and be diligent in the reading at dawn and diligent in the reading at the evening hour, and in your services of dawn and evening,
and perform them completely and patiently, not being troubled by the one who troubles you; for it is written,
"Whoever troubles you will bear the judgment, whoever he may be,"
so that the written word may call you blessed: "Blessed is the nation whose God is the Lord, the people whom the Lord has chosen as his inheritance."
And the word of scripture will call you more blessed still: "Blessed is the people that knows the shout of joy.

Lord, they will walk in the light of your face, and rejoice in your name all day long, and be exalted in your righteousness. For you are the boast of their strength. He whom mercy has exalted in your righteousness [?]."
And so that you too may be able to speak boldly in this: "Our protector is the Lord; the Holy One of Israel is our king."

O blessed are those of our kind who will be called blessed on earth by the mouths of thousands, and who will be called blessed in heaven as well, by the mouths of ten thousands upon ten thousands in the heavens.

O woe indeed to those of our way of life in the congregations of God whom the people of earth call blessed, while those of heaven treat them as strangers because of their works—and they are a great many.
Woe to those of whom the people of earth say, "It is they," while those of heaven say of them, "It is not they."
Woe to those who dwell in the house of God, his congregations and his holy places, of whom the people of earth say,
"They are children of God," while those of heaven say, "Not so; they are children of darkness and enemies of God," because of their evil works.
Above all those who do these evil works, defiled and polluted in the house of Christ: is it only the people on earth who matter to them [?]—
above all, will they be hidden from those of heaven? As it is written,
"What is crooked cannot be adorned, and what is lacking cannot be counted."
O blessed are those of our way of life who will trust in their innocence, as our holy father
said many times in his holy letters.
Woe, woe to those who do not have this, and do not possess it in the congregations of God.
O blessed are those who hope in a hope of their own, knowing that it pleases God and is acceptable to Christ, because of their wisdom
and their conduct, having gained for themselves a hope in heaven and an unspeakable wealth forever.

And woe to those who have no hope in heaven and do not know in what they believe—what are these works for, these works again [?]—who, because of their folly and their disobedience, such people as these, have gained for themselves poverty and misery,
and weeping and mourning forever down in Amente.
So, brothers, since we know what we ought to do in these few swift days to complete it, as it is written by another saint, "For my life is swifter than a runner,"
let us not forget, nor let us be negligent, for they will not give us another day.
When each one's days are completed—if we were to speak, we would have much to say about the misery of those who were negligent.

And again, if we were to speak, we would have much to say about those who will become rich through their diligence, by carrying out their work successfully and healing themselves through repentance after they have fallen. For the matter rests with every person on earth, at every time, who wants to be saved.
But it is our hardness of heart and our disobedience that make us unworthy of these things. For indeed it is written,
"Unless the Lord builds a house, those who build it labor in vain,"
and "Unless the Lord guards a city, the one who guards it keeps watch in vain."

Again, "No one can say 'Jesus is Lord' except by a holy Spirit." And again, the Lord of glory, Jesus, says, "Without me you can do nothing." Does it not follow, then, that unless God works with a person, the person cannot work alone toward his salvation? For when a person works with God in good deeds and good works,

God too works with him in every blessing and makes him grow in the fruits of righteousness [?] according to his hope in God from the beginning, God having set him after him in the things you read [?].
So, too, he now says, "It is I, it is I; and when you grow old, it is still I." Christ Jesus is the same yesterday,
and today, and forever.
O blessed are those who understand, and who come into the midst of the good and the evil: the evil, so as to guard themselves
against it; the good, so as to accomplish it with gladness.
It is written,
after all, "It is a cheerful giver whom God loves."

What, then, is a giver? Not only one who gives bread or clothing to his neighbor, but in everything you do in works of righteousness, you should accomplish them with gladness: whether prayer, or ascetic discipline, or purity of heart and purity of body—that you do them all with gladness—or blessing God day and night; that you know for whom you are doing them, and also that you know from whom you will receive their reward, knowing
that whoever would draw near to God must believe that he exists, and that he will be the rewarder of those who seek him.
Let us not, then, be negligent in the season of sowing, so that we may find something to reap or to gather.
Many people labor in vain without understanding how to keep watch over themselves, and the written word will be fulfilled upon them: "Why do you toil,
when your labor does not satisfy?"
So it is that there is nothing new under the sun: these things have been tested.
They were tested from the beginning,
and they were written down for us as instruction by those who had been taught,
with whom the Lord spoke.
For I have already said this many times:
it is not just one sin that stands against a person, but a great many.
Not only is hatred of others accursed, as has been written about it,
but injustice is more accursed still.
That is why scripture says, "Let everyone who names the name of the Lord turn away from injustice."

So, too, our holy father never tired of speaking about slander in his holy letters, saying these things and others: "Woe to those who are companions to one another in slander, running to one another with great eagerness to carry it out together."
I say this, wretched and poor as I am: just as with the eagerness of those who run to one another with a great burning, through the devil, to commit fornication,
so it is with those who run to one another to commit slander.
For indeed I have said these things many times concerning the ruin of such people, who destroy their hope
at a single stroke and squander their labors, gaining no profit at all from all their labor because of their mouths and their ears.
Is it not written, "Whoever says, 'I worship God,' and does not bridle his tongue, his worship is worthless"?

For whoever is a companion in slander and whispering is a companion in fornication without knowing it. The one who commits fornication and the woman with whom he commits it keep looking this way and that in agitation, lest people see them, until they have committed their fornication.
So, too, the slanderer and the listener draw themselves off to one side alone, looking this way and that, agitated lest people hear them, until they have committed their slander.
That is why both are cursed alike by God, these and the others: those who fornicate and those who slander.
For indeed the slanderer is no different from the fornicator, and the fornicator is no different from the slanderer.
For just as, when a man's heart is full of defilement
and burns for fornication, he cannot carry it out according to his wicked desire unless he finds a woman who will commit fornication with him,
or else he carries out his desires in other, unnatural ways with those he finds ready for such conduct—these and the others who are accursed—
so it is with slander as well.

Even if the heart of the ungodly man is full of defilement, he still cannot carry out his impurity with his mouth unless he finds someone like himself in that same corner, who burns to hear evil about his neighbor and his disgrace,
so that the listener may take delight, like the prostitute who takes delight in pleasure with those who commit fornication with her.
In this way the listener to slander is pleased, so that the slanderer rises up beside him
and does not keep silent, but despises his neighbor. To what, then, shall we compare this one and that one?
The speaker and the listener are like Satan and lawlessness, and lawlessness and Satan. Or perhaps, indeed, is the listener not worse than the slanderer?
In this way the listener looks on after the other has risen up beside him, as he pours out all his fornication with his mouth into the listener's ears,

just as the fornicator who pours out all his fornication with his mouth into the listener's ears—just as the fornicator who commits all his fornication in the bosom of the wicked woman—keeps looking out in the burning of his wicked heart to see whether there is yet another coming to whom he may tell it, as he told the one who rose up with him,
so that he may take even greater delight in despising a crowd of people better than himself. And just like the prostitute who shows herself in the streets, who is a snare

to a crowd of wretches: after this one has risen up beside her and committed his fornication with her, she looks out again for another, or for others, to see who will come upon her, those who are like her in that same corner,
this one and that one, so that they may commit fornication with her. If people of this kind had [?] the labor of the things that please God,
it would have been better if people of this kind had sought only their glory, and if the slanderer and the listener had boasted in it,
rather than seeking the disgrace of their neighbors and the contempt of their fellow ministers of God—of the one God whom they worship and of the one Lord whom they serve;
rather than rejoicing with a joy full of weeping without knowing it, and delighting with a false joy over the disgrace of their neighbors, a joy full of mourning they do not perceive.
What the devil wants is the very thing these people love, and what the demons rejoice over
is the very thing they rejoice in.
Indeed, our holy father said this too, in anger and wrath from God:
that it is said of two kinds of creatures that they cast out their desire through their mouths.
One kind, he said, is among the birds that live in the waters, and the other is found among the creeping things on the earth.
"Such," he said, "are people of this kind: the slanderer and the listener who is pleased."
What, then, is the portion of these, or what is the lot of the others,

when all the words of wrath in scripture, which it spoke from God, come upon them: "I cast out the one who slanders his neighbor in secret," or "You sat slandering your brother, and you laid a stumbling block for your mother's son.
You did these things, and I kept silent.
You conceived lawlessness [?]
…that I would be like you.
I will rebuke you and set them before your face. Understand these things, then, you who forget God, he says.
Recognize now what you are despising [?] in these things, lest he seize you and there be no one to save you.
"A sacrifice of praise will glorify me," he says, not slander. God forbid! "This is the way that I will teach you, so that [I may show you?] the salvation of God."
Oh, what will happen when the words of Scripture stand against us before the judgment seat of Christ? For this is truly how it will be.
Do you not know, poor wretched man, that what you sow will grow, and what you cast into the earth will spring up?
If the good Savior said that the kingdom of heaven is like
a grain of mustard seed, which a man took and sowed in his field, and which is smaller than all seeds,
yet when it grows it becomes a great plant and turns into a great tree, so that the birds of heaven come and nest in its branches,
then this is how it is: when you sow good fruit in the earth, it springs up into many good fruits, which are sweet and useful to people.
In the same way, when you sow bad fruit in the earth,
it grows up hostile and harms those who walk by. If you plant a date stone in the earth, does it not spring up in many ways?

It and all the other trees that are good and choice in the garden: their owner waits for them through so many seasons [?], tends them, and watches for their fruit, because it is good to eat and useful to people.
So too with the vine, which is tended because its wine is useful,
and because it is a joy to those who drink it, especially to the sick.
But look also at the seeds of the thornbush when you sow them in the earth, and weeds, and every hostile wild tree: see how they spring up, though their owners do not wait any seasons for them.
Nor do they watch for their fruit. Even fools already understand what we are saying, and need no explanation of it.
The fruit of those who do works of righteousness on earth is known from what we have said, and the fruit of those who do works of lawlessness on earth is likewise known from what we have said.
Now since the devil knows, being cunning,
that man is strong and able to prevail on the road by which he will go to the one who made him, he does all he can [?] to ensnare many of those who will obey him.
Oh, you are accursed, devil, because of the many nets, each different from the others, that you have devised in your evil heart,

making their scent smell sweet [?] in the hearts of the senseless, who hate their own souls, fools who do not love their own souls so that they [?], until you make them strangers to life. How many could one list, and how many would one leave out? [?]

But this snare in particular you have laid for those who bear the name and the habit, and who are in the places of Christ, and above all for those throughout the whole earth who wish to draw near to God.

It is hidden, and harder than all your snares, just as idolatry and the heretics are, for you have darkened their hearts until you lead them astray and make them blind, so that they do not know God who created them.
I am speaking of hatred, slander and envy, with which you have entangled [?] them in secret.
Scripture cries out: "Whoever slanders his brother or judges his brother slanders the law
and judges the law. But if you judge the law, you are not a doer of the law."
Truly, whoever slanders his neighbor is like many works of lawlessness. He is like a fornicator, as we said before,
and he is like a thief in what he does: like the shame of a thief
when he is caught, as the words of Scripture say, with the stolen goods in his hand.
This, too, is how the shame of a slanderer is,
and of the one who listens, when the person the slander is about comes upon them, or overhears them without their knowing, after they have finished all their wickedness

and the words of envy and hatred in their mouths, and they look this way and see him standing there, having listened to them without their knowing, and they look behind them and see that he has heard all they have said.
Do you not know how
their faces change and their hearts melt? So we may know that the lot of the thief
is the lot of the slanderer and of the one who listens.

If your face changed and your heart melted because the person whose slander you were speaking heard you, how greatly will you be troubled, how full of shame will your face be, at the time when those whom you do not know come for you
and carry you before the one you have never seen, Christ, for him to punish you according to your works: he who loved mankind, he who was cursed and did not curse,

who offered himself up as a holy sacrifice to his Father, not for one or two, nor for a single nation, but for the whole world, for those who wish to be saved; who gave us boldness and allowed us to call upon him at all times.
Know how he speaks with you, O man, and his love toward all people alike, as he taught us to call upon him and his Father when he taught us to pray: "Our Father who is in heaven."
He did not tell you to say, "My Father" only, but "Our Father who is in heaven, hallowed be your name;
your kingdom come;
your will be done; as it is in heaven, so may it be on earth;
our bread that is to come," he says.
Nor did he allow you to say, "My bread that is to come, give it to me today," but "Our bread that is to come, give it to us today."
"Forgive us our debts," he says.
He did not tell you to say, "Forgive me my debts," but "as we also forgive those who are indebted to us."
You are not one person alone in your prayer; rather, with your mouth you bear witness for a multitude, that they forgive those who are indebted to them.
"And do not lead us into temptation."
You are one, yet you pray for many in what the Savior, the lover of mankind, has put into your mouth.
"But deliver us from the evil one, for yours is the power and the glory forever and ever. Amen."
See the love of Christ, as we said before, making his whole creation one in their prayer, wishing us to love one another, whether we eat together or walk,
or go to church, or receive the body and blood of the Lord, being of one unity and love and one mind in Christ, praying for one another in love,
just as he taught us to pray, so that he might accept it from us, deliver us from the evil one, and grant us the kingdom of heaven;
and that we should forgive every grievance in our heart against our neighbor, so that he too may forgive us,
so that we may not be liars in our prayer: "Forgive us, as we forgive those who are indebted to us."
And again: "If anyone has a complaint against another, just as Christ forgave you,
so you also must do." And again: "If you forgive people their sins, your Father who is in heaven will also forgive you your sins.
For if you do not forgive people their sins," he says, "neither will your Father forgive you your sins."
What do we have now? Envy, hatred and slander,
and above all defilements, pollutions, violence and greed, and all the other abominable works of the devil and his demons, though God and his Christ
have chosen us to be sons to him in the kingdom of heaven, so that we may inherit with Christ for ages of ages, in all glory and every blessing forever.
What have we to do now with the devil and his demons, that they should be punished with him in Amente, in the fire of Gehenna and the worm that does not sleep, when we are not of him?
What now? It is not of us; rather, we are of God.
For he is the one who breathed into our face a breath of life, and we have become one with him through the body and blood of his holy Son,
which he has graciously given us, so that we have become one sonship with the Holy Trinity, whether small or great, male or female, everyone who receives the body and blood of the Lord.
We have become one with God,
not as gods, God forbid!
but as sons of their holy Father, and as brothers of the blessed Christ, the King of heaven and earth,

according to what he said with his truthful mouth: "Whoever does the will of my Father who is in heaven"; when they asked him, "Look, your mother and your brothers are standing outside, wanting to speak with you," he answered the one who said it to him, "Who is my mother,
and who are my brothers? For whoever does the will of my Father who is in heaven is my brother and my sister and my mother."
Since, then, we have these promises, beloved,
let us purify ourselves from every defilement of flesh and spirit, perfecting purity in the fear of God the Lord,
as our apostle said, "giving no cause of stumbling in anything, so that the ministry may not be blamed,"
just as he also said this.
Blessed are you, Lord God Almighty,
the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who created all things through his beloved holy Son.
Blessed are you, Jesus Christ,
and blessed is the Holy Spirit, the counselor with his holy Father, giving every blessing upon the earth,
and every mercy and compassion upon the earth, and patience and forbearance.
For if you do not forgive us, God Almighty, and if you do not cover our sins, Jesus Christ, we are worthless before you,
and we will not be able to appear before you at all.

But we beseech you, God of powers, who worked all wonders in Israel from the beginning for the sake of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, to do so with us now as well, for the sake of your holy name and for the sake of your beloved holy Son Jesus, our Savior and our life,
and not to bring us to account, for we are flesh, and

we are earth, as you said from the beginning to the first man, Adam: "You are earth, and you will return to earth." Forgive us, for we are the clay and the work of your hands. Have compassion on us, God of powers, and forgive us, for we are grass, as you said by the mouth of your prophets: "All flesh is grass."
You are the God of powers, through whom every power exists. You created the earth as if it were nothing [?], and those who dwell in it are like grasshoppers before you.
They are reckoned as spittle [?], and like a drop falling from a bucket, and like the tipping of a scale, according to the words of your prophets.
O God of powers and Lord of glory, Jesus, if you do not have compassion on us, who will have compassion on us? If you do not have mercy on us, who will have mercy on us?
For you know our weakness and our feebleness, and the infirmity of our body is not hidden from you. Blessed are you, Lord, and holy, and blessed is the name of your holy glory forever and ever.
Of John: Exegesis.
In the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, the consubstantial and indivisible Trinity.
We believe in the begetting of the only-begotten Son from his Father before the foundation of the world. We believe in the birth of our Savior from the Virgin Mary, who remains a virgin at all times.
We believe in the sufferings that our Savior endured for us on the cross, which is full of salvation.
We believe in his resurrection from the dead.
We believe in his ascension into heaven.
We hope to receive the forgiveness of our sins through his holy body and his true blood.
After this canon of the holy Apa John had been read in the whole church and they had finished, knowing that it is of benefit [?] for all,
the Lord gave it to us in a small book written of old.
We copied it so that it might be remembered forever.

We have placed it under the authority of our fathers who are in the desert, so that it may remain under the authority of the church on the mountain of the Virgin Mary, in the days when Father [?] Mena and Paeit [?] Zacharias were its stewards, so that everyone who seeks this holy canon may receive it from them, be comforted by its words, and return it to them,
so that this great and perfect archimandrite Apa John may show grace to them and to the one who took care of it [?], and make him worthy of the places of rest that are in heaven,
and write their names in the book of life. Amen. So be it, so be it [?].
The rich will glorify the One who is rich in mercy when they stretch out their hands in mercy toward those in need who share this same nature as you.
The poor will glorify her who bore the one who became poor for our sake of his own will, so that he might make us rich in works of righteousness.
Servants will glorify her who bore the one who emptied himself, taking the form of a servant for our sake, when they show genuine service toward their masters according to the flesh,
and above all toward the commandments of our Lord, all of us alike.
We priests will glorify her who bore for us the priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek, when we purify ourselves,
as it is written: "Let the priests who draw near to God purify themselves, lest the Lord destroy some of them,"
fearing greatly, too, lest we be found drawing nearer to him here than anyone else
yet farther from him than anyone else in the other place because of our sins.
But all of us together, whether priests or people,

let us entreat and pray with all our heart to her who is able to intercede for us before God more than all the saints, the holy Theotokos Mary, whom God has glorified in heaven and on earth above all creation,
visible and invisible, that she may intercede for us before her Son, the true God,
that he may cover the sins we have committed up to now in the great sea of his love for mankind,
and take away from us this heart of stone [?]
[?] demons, so that they too may inherit with him the fire and the worm.
How do they differ from him now in Amente,
all those who have gone down into it from the beginning until now, and those who will yet go down into it until the end of the age, according to the measure of each one's sins?
What, then, is the difference between the devil with his demons, and Judas with all the sinners who will die in their sins without repenting? Do they differ from one another at all
in the fire of Gehenna?

We wish to know whether sinners do not differ from one another, or from the devil and his demons, in Amente, and whether Greeks and heretics, barbarians and Jews, who do not believe in the Lord Jesus, are of one likeness with one another in the fire and the worm that does not sleep.
Look at a place that is very deep and exceedingly dry, and take some of every good kind of wood,
of all the choice woods of Lebanon,
and of every wood that is on earth, of every kind, down to thorns and brambles;

and [?] them all, take some of every one of them and throw them into the deep, dry place, and set fire to it, with a wind blowing on them by God's command; and see whether the appearance of their smoke and their burning differ from one another in any way.
For even fools already understand,
and need nothing more in this example: this is what those in Amente are like.
For they are in the midst of the [?] in the fire,
and beneath them is the worm that does not sleep, for God created the worm that is in Amente
and the [?],
which are immortal,
just like the unquenchable fire, to punish the devil and his demons in Amente by means of the fire that is not quenched.
In the same way we have learned this from the acts of the holy martyrs: that he does not spare any of those we have mentioned,
as we have found it, punishing them all and condemning them to death according to the tenor of his decrees, which are written in the acts of the martyrs.
As is written in his letters: "Whoever among the great bishops of the country is willing to obey my edict, which I have sent out,
and to worship the gods,
will receive great authority, not only in their own city
but in the whole country.
But if they do not obey my edict," he says,
"and do not worship the gods,
they shall be condemned to death." And this is how the holy martyrs endured until they received the crown of life.
We have said these things because, if the king, to whom God gave authority to reign on earth,
inspires fear of this kind, and wrath with great threats against those who turn away from his decrees,
those who oppose his edict, so that he punishes them with swords and many other tortures, as is written,
"the wrath of a king is like the roaring of a lion", though he teaches godlessness and [destroys?] souls by the multitude [?];
if he has threats of this kind
and a wrath that cannot be appeased with money,
how much more the King of heaven and earth, the Creator of all,
who created all things out of what did not exist, the heavens and the earth,
the sea and all that is in them: will he not be angry?

Or can anyone withstand the fury of his wrath against any person, whether man or woman, small or great, priest or monk, king or ruler, or any leader of the people, who turns away from the decrees of the Lord and his law, his ordinances, his judgments and his testimonies, which he testified to us from the beginning by the mouth of his holy prophets and by the mouth of his holy only-begotten Son Jesus? As the apostle says: "In many parts and in many ways God spoke of old to our fathers in the prophets;
but at the end of these days he has spoken to us in the Son,
whom he made heir of all things,
through whom he also created the ages";

and also by the mouth of his apostles. What, then, will become of people like these? Or who will be able to appease the fury of the wrath of God, the King of heaven and earth, who teaches true godliness, that people should not worship wood and stone,
as did the kings who went mad, of whom we have spoken concerning the fear and the fury of their wrath,
those who teach people to worship wood and stone and all the other
works of human hands? But the Lord teaches that he is to be worshiped in spirit and truth, because he alone is the true God,
as it is written: "God is spirit, and those who worship him must worship him in spirit and truth";
and also that he is to be served, because he is the King of heaven and earth,
and it was he who created them when they did not exist, whether angels or principalities or authorities or all who are in heaven, for they all came into being through him.
So you see, we know: woe to every kind of person
who does not keep the decrees of the Lord from the holy Scriptures.
The kings we have spoken of, who turned away [?] from the truth,
punish bodies with the sword,
or with fire and other tortures, but the soul they cannot overpower;
they cannot even see it,
nor do they know what it is like within a person.
Rather, it goes out in secret and passes into the hands of God, and he gives it what it deserves.
But God punishes both the soul and the body of those who disobey him in the fire of Gehenna in Amente.
O only true God
and Lord of glory, Jesus, we have no word to say before you if you judge us and bring us to account
according to the measure of our evils. But you will forgive for the sake of your name alone, because it is holy
and glorious forever.
Woe to every person who neglects to turn from sin until he dies,
as we have said many times.
What, then, have those who neglect it until they die in defilement not lost?

They have lost being escorted gloriously by the angels on the day of their visitation, who greet them with joy and sing hymns with them with a voice of gladness and rejoicing, as it is written: "These things I remembered, and I poured out my soul within me,
for I will go into the place of the wonderful tabernacle,
to the house of God, with a voice of rejoicing and thanksgiving, the sound of those keeping festival."
"Why are you sorrowful, my soul?" he says,
"and why do you trouble me?
Hope in God, for I will give thanks to him; the salvation of my face is my God."
For indeed, according to what our father David says, this is not for David alone,

according to what the Lord said in the Gospel, that they will be like the angels in heaven: those who have kept them and set that age before their eyes while they were on earth, doing good as it deserves.
And you have lost, O you of whom we are speaking
(you know who they are, as we do [?]),
you who died in sin before you came out of it, you have lost the paradise of God's delight, [?] adorned [?], and the beauty of the fruit and its sweetness,
and the chance to taste of them; and the tree in the middle of paradise, because of which death came into the world, though there would now be no work of death because of it
from that time on.

You have lost, too, the sight of the tree of life, so that you might eat of its fruit, just as the righteous and all the saints will eat of the tree of life [?] prayer to God [?] the righteous and all the saints:
"that you will feed us from the tree of life,
and raise us in your holy first resurrection with your apostles and your prophets and your righteous ones and all your saints."
And you have lost the true rising in the first resurrection with the righteous and all the saints,
by which you too would have come in their honor and glory with Christ
and his righteous ones and all the saints at the end of the age.
For indeed there is no greater loss,
and no grief greater, than that of those who died without forsaking sin or coming out of it until they came into the hands of Amente.
But I will go on again to speak with grief about those among the dead who have gone down into it
and those who [?]
Because of the good he does for us: that is, his great forbearance, in that he has not wiped us out, nor those who do evil on the earth among those who do good before him.
But the time of the harvest is coming, when he will gather the good into it, to their place of rest.

And he will also gather the wicked through the holy angels, to cast them down into Amente, into the fire of Gehenna, or rather out into the outer darkness, the place where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
It is fitting for us to be instructed, like all those who have been instructed by the many words of the Scriptures, which have called us to repentance from the beginning.
When a beast is trained to walk from its youth, it does not change its gait, unless through weakness, until its old age.
But we have been taught the works of our salvation, that is, the works through which we shall be saved,
and yet we forget them.
Or if we do learn them at one time, at another time we pay them no attention.
If the goad is in the hand of the one who drives the beast, it is afraid and walks its road well.
Much more are the words of Scripture a goad for a person, that we should listen to them and improve our conduct in everything, according to what pleases God.
Or does Scripture not say, "A whip for the horse, a goad for the donkey, and a rod for a foolish nation"? What is the rod of the foolish nation, if not the words of the Scriptures? As it is written:
"He who brings wisdom out of his mouth strikes a foolish man with a rod."
O the great grief of heart I am about to speak of! It is a shame for us, we who neglect to listen to God as he calls us,

saying, "Turn away from your sins and come to me with even a little good, and I will receive you to myself; I will be a father to you, and you will be sons and daughters to me, says the Lord, the Almighty."
Is the snake not an evil beast? And yet with a little [?], when the charmer charms it,

reptiles that are wild beasts of this kind lay aside the wildness of their nature and take on a tameness contrary to their nature, and come out into the hands of the one who charms them with great tameness, because of the few words they have heard from the charmer's mouth.

But we, whose hearts have been shut against them, have not listened to all the words of the Scriptures, those of the Old and those of the New and those of all the saints, especially those of our holy father, though they all call us to forsake the sins that are contrary to our nature, through which we shall die, and to do the good things that accord with our nature, through which we shall be saved.

And we have not listened even to this day, but have become like a deaf snake that stops its ears, so as not to hear the voice of those who charm it, or a charm prepared by a wise man, according to the Scriptures,
until wrath comes and we have still not come out of our evil ways.
We who commit iniquities cannot bear the anger of God's wrath, though we provoke him at all times with our evil deeds, especially we who dwell in the places of Christ, priests and monks.
O how great is the shame that will be ours on the day of our visitation, if we do not quickly remove these things from us!
As it is written, "He who does not heal himself in his works is the brother of the one who destroys himself."

"A fool, when he asks, will have it counted to him as wisdom." And again, wishing to praise those who will forsake their sins and repent quickly, it says, "He who heals himself in his works: the name of the Lord is revealed in the greatness of his strength;
and the righteous will be exalted in running to it," to show his kindness toward everyone who will forsake their sins and not return to them from this moment on.
Or do you not know that it is a great grief before God when people sin in his holy places, especially if they do not quickly forsake their sins?

If God said to Moses at that time, when he spoke with him at the bush, "Take the sandals off your feet, for the place on which you are standing is holy ground," though it was only a mountain, then what will he say to us, who dwell in his holy places? "Take off from yourselves all these iniquities: impurities and defilements, thefts and lies, envy and hatred, quarrels and strife, and all the other sins that are abominable before me, for the place in which you dwell is holy ground,
and I dwell in it." [?] The saints have proclaimed this about it, as he said through the prophet:
"Turn away from all malice, violence and robbery, so that we may have no word to speak against me."
For indeed the commander-in-chief of the host of the Lord, when he appeared to Joshua as he kept watch at Jericho, did not hold back from saying to him,
"Take the sandals off your feet, for the place on which you are standing is holy ground."

Again, to show what we have said: why is it not fitting for us, who remain dwelling in the places of Christ while being disobedient to his holy law, to break quickly the bonds of all iniquity and cast them off from us,
so that he who is in heaven will laugh at them,

and the Lord will mock them, speaking to them in his wrath and troubling them in his anger, so that the enemy and his abominable demons may no longer hinder or prevent those who wish to come out of their sins and repent quickly,
so that they may receive a blessing from the Lord and mercy from God our Savior,
and it may be said, "This is the generation of those who seek the Lord, who seek the face of the God of Jacob"?
O how great is our shame,
we who do not listen to all these words, until the five days in which we live come to an end for us,
and our portion is with all those who were disobedient from the beginning, who disregarded the words of those who desired their salvation and counseled them to do good,
and paid it no attention at all, until they went down to Amente!
If you do not know your portion, O you who will die in your sins, especially in the places of Christ, we will tell you of it according to all the words of the Scriptures.
Your portion is the portion of Cain, who was the first to receive the curse from the mouth of God on the earth, because he did not listen to the teaching of his fathers,
nor did he emulate the deeds and good works of his brother Abel the righteous, but prepared for himself vengeance from God forever.
So we too have not listened to the words of the Scriptures,
to remove our evil deeds from us and do good things, so that God may have mercy on us.
Nor again have we emulated the deeds and good works of our righteous brothers who dwell with us, so that we have prepared for ourselves vengeance and an everlasting retribution forever in Amente.
You are counted with those whom the Lord wiped out by a flood of water in the beginning, because they took to evil from their youth,

and the earth was filled with violence through them, according to the words of Scripture, since they did not listen to Noah the righteous as he counseled them, he who built himself an ark for the saving of his household; through it he condemned the world and became an heir of the righteousness that comes by faith.

Was it not just as the word says, "Through it he condemned the world"? He condemned the world because they saw him building the ark, three hundred cubits long, fifty cubits wide and thirty cubits high, building it with [?], with lower, second and third stories, coating it inside
and outside with pitch, signifying to them that a flood would come upon the earth, for he had become a herald of righteousness, as it is written.
And they did not listen to him, until they met a death of grief and wrath at the hands of the one they had angered, God the Almighty,
and until this great, all-sweeping destruction came upon the earth,

with no son to protect the body of his father and bury him, nor any father to protect his sons and cover them amid the waters, when the deep burst open and the floodgates of heaven were opened; nor were there wives to protect their husbands,
nor husbands to protect their wives, nor brothers to protect brothers.
But this single destruction came upon them all at once; nor was there a memorial offering going up for them in remembrance of them,

or tears and prayers as a sacrifice in memory of those who had died. Instead they were all wiped out in destruction, except Noah alone, who was left with his wife and his sons in the ark, and who offered up offerings on the altar after he came out of the ark; and the Lord smelled a sweet savor.
He had mercy and established with him an everlasting covenant.
So we too have not taken heed [?] of those whom he destroyed before us among the people of old.

Nor have we emulated our brothers who do good in hunger and thirst, in long fasts, in many vigils many times, in purity (the great chief point of which we are speaking), in renunciation, and in all the good works they perform, which bear witness to their love for God, since he too, the Lord, the good Savior, loved them all the more, even to death,
the death of the cross, while they do these things and others, and we look at them as we live with them.
We have not taken heed.
Nor have we heard that there will be an end no different from the water of the flood; I mean death.

Just as the giants of old and all the people it destroyed did not wish to see Noah and all his household, whom it saved, so sinful people, or lawless brothers, will not wish to see righteous brothers in their rest and their joy, when they themselves die in their evil deeds.
Again, you are counted with Pharaoh and all his host, who sank in the Red Sea
because they disobeyed God
as he spoke to them through the holy prophet Moses and through Aaron.

You are counted with those whom the Lord struck down in the desert with various deaths, because they disobeyed him and did not act according to all that he had commanded them, as they walked with the people of God at that time, whom God protected until he brought them into the land of their inheritance.
You are counted with the company of Korah, Dathan and Abiram, for whom the earth split open:
they went down to Amente alive with their whole company,
especially if you commit transgressions: impurities, defilements and things against nature.
Your inheritance and your lot will be with the people of Sodom and Gomorrah.
You are counted with all those who plotted against the Lord Jesus until they killed him.
You are counted with those who rejected all the words of the prophets from the beginning.
You are counted with those who rejected the teaching of the apostles
and despised them.
You are counted with all those who have denied [?] the sound faith from the beginning, for whom no memorial of blessedness has remained.
You are counted with the pagans and the heretics.
You are counted with the murderous barbarians. For we have not spoken a single word that will not come to pass.
Our holy father, through whom God spoke, said in his holy letters:

"If a pagan, or a heretic, or a murderous gentile turns to God, how much more readily will God receive him than a brother of this kind, who commits these abominations in his holy places while wearing the holy name of God and the habit!"
Or else why do you not know, you fools who are not wise,
that whoever dies in his sins
is taken down to Amente, no different from any of those we have spoken of,
for they are in Amente?
And again he informed us of this other thing in his holy writings:
that all the sinners who have died from Cain until now, and those who will die until the end of the age, are taken down to Amente, as the Gospel says.
Or does Scripture not say to us,
"If God did not spare the ancient world, if God did not spare the angels when they sinned"?
He did not spare those who walked with Moses in the desert at that time, but repaid them;
he did not spare the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah, but burned them;
he did not spare false prophets and false apostles;
he did not spare anyone who sins in any way, from the beginning of creation until now, but cast them down into Amente,
just as the Scriptures bear witness to what we are saying.
Will he then spare us because we are clothed in a habit,
and because we have the form of godliness while denying its power?
Shall we say,
"Why should we be put to shame before our holy fathers and our holy brothers who have gone to God, and all those who will go to him in holiness until the end of the age?"
Arise, let us repent, O brothers,
while there is time,
so that we may attain what the Lord has said:
"An hour is coming, and it is now, when the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God, and those who will [?]
